newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty climbs vs basket, but outlook bearish.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty climbs vs basket, but outlook bearish.

text.p: The Polish zloty recouped morning losses against the basket of currencies and closed stronger than on Tuesday as banks shortened currency positions in late trade on Wednesday, dealers said.
They said, however, that the trend would likely reverse on Thursday because foreign investors were looking to purchase dollars after their Polish T-bills were sold or matured.

"Banks cut positions today in order to benefit from holding zlotys over the weekend, during which the local currency is not devalued, but the trend will probably reverse on Thursday," said Bogdan Stepkowski of ING Bank in Warsaw.
The zloty closed at 1.61/1.55 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than Tuesday's 1.51/1.46 percent.
The local currency was at 2.7832/42 to the dollar, down from 2.7770/85 on Tuesday and at 1.8420/35 to the mark, up from yesterday's 1.8470/80.
Dealers said that many foreign investors, which exited from the Polish debt market refrained from purchasing dollars today because of the zloty's relative weakness against the basket.
The zloty has remained boxed in between 1.9 and 1.6 percent from parity for months before dipping below 1.5 percent on Tuesday on the back of a dollar surge on international markets.
On the money market overnight and tomorrow/next deposit rates held flat at 19.20/19.35 and 19.20/19.40 percent respectively as the market remained short-of-cash.
Dealers said the shortage caused the central bank to raise its main 14-day drainage rate by 0.02 point to 19.15 percent.
Dealers said the market's cash shortage also caused some banks to sell T-bills on the secondary market, which combined with foreign investor sales, pulled up T-bill yields.
In afternoon trade three-month paper was quoted at 19.50 percent, up from this morning's 19.10 percent.
